messages:
scan-bot: nightly SAST+DAST finished. new failures in auth/keystore service. tagging: @maria @ashley

maria: seeing multiple CI flakes that look like KMS permission errors, plus a couple of high-confidence SAST alerts around keystore API usage. paste of failing job: 
```
[ci] run: ./scripts/invoke-keystore-test.sh
ERROR: kms.Decrypt: permission denied
  at keystore.decrypt (keystore.go:142)
  at auth.Init (auth.go:78)
```

ashley: oof. did we push the RBAC change to the service account yesterday? devops-lead rolled out a keystore-policy tweak at 02:10 UTC.

devops-lead: yep, I changed the keystore KMS binding to remove a legacy service account; added an ephemeral role for deployer-ephemeral. the change was intended to limit broad decrypt rights. I can roll it back but want to understand why tests fail only intermittently.

lin: might be a timing/ephemeral grant race during CI parallel runs. CI jobs rely on an ephemeral grant from the grants service; if the grant isn't issued before keystore.Init, we hit permission denied.

security-oncall: this also flagged 2 SAST findings: one is low (hardcoded path check), one medium (keystore usage without strict context auth). I posted the SAST reports to the artifact store: https://ci.internal/reports/1738001234/sast.json

maria: linking the DAST result too — the auth endpoint returned a 500 on malformed input which tripped the keystore call path. DAST may be exploring edge inputs that expose the crypto path.

ashley: can we reproduce locally? steps?

maria: run with docker-compose (keystore in devmode) + simulated CI env: 
```bash
CI=true JOB_ID=local-1 ./scripts/ci-run-keystore.sh
# repro yields same kms.Decrypt permission denied about 30% of runs
```

devops-lead: for immediate mitigation I suggest: 1) temporarily reapply previous KMS binding (quick rollback) 2) add a short retry loop in keystore.Init while we confirm grant timing 3) add an audit hook to log KMS decision and request identity. thoughts?

lin: agree on retry + audit. retries short-circuit will avoid long CI delays. also add metadata to the audit log: grant_id & iam_principal. that helps triage who requested the ephemeral grant.

security-oncall: audit logs are critical here. we need to ensure CloudAudit includes KMS.Decrypt ALLOW/DENY entries forwarded to log-indexer. right now we have 7-day retention for debug logs; we should increase to 30 days for keystore-related keystreams until this is resolved. I can open retention ticket.

maria: noted. for the SAST finding (keystore usage without context auth) I think it's a code smell: we should ensure the keystore API requires a request-scoped principal (not global service token). adding that check will also reduce blast radius if a grant is misapplied.

ashley: quick checklist I can run: 
- revert KMS binding in prod and staging (devops-lead)
- add retry+instrumentation to keystore.Init (maria + lin)
- increase audit retention & add filter for KMS.Decrypt (security-oncall)
- run targeted DAST on auth endpoint after rollback (sre-bot)

devops-lead: rolling back to previous binding in staging now. will keep prod untouched until we confirm. staging rollback started at 1738001300.

sre-bot: scheduled targeted DAST run: https://scans.internal/run/1738001234?target=auth-staging — will report back.

lin: quick patch I pushed to feature/keystore-retry with short exponential backoff and instrumented log lines: 
```go
// in keystore.Init
for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
  err := kmsClient.Decrypt(ctx, req)
  if err == nil { return nil }
  log.Warnf("kms.Decrypt failed: %v (attempt %d)", err, i+1)
  time.Sleep(time.Millisecond * 200 * (1<<i))
}
return fmt.Errorf("kms.Decrypt permanently failed")
```

maria: that will suppress transient CI flakes. but we still must fix the grant lifecycle. can we make the grants service synchronous for CI jobs (block until grant confirmed) or add a pre-warm step?

devops-lead: good call — I can add a pre-warm hook to the CI pipeline that requests and verifies the ephemeral grant before the main job starts. cheap fix.

security-oncall: also propose we add a scanning rule to SAST to flag cases where keystore.Decrypt is called before request context has authenticated principal. that helps prevent future code patterns that mask identity checks. I'll add an entry to the scanning rules backlog.

ashley: for the medium SAST finding, can we mitigate with a PR-level quick fix (validate ctx.Principal != nil) + unit test?

maria: yes, prepping a PR for that now. will include test that simulates missing principal and ensures error path avoids calling KMS.

devops-lead: staging rollback completed at 1738001365. staging DAST started after rollback.

sre-bot: DAST run finished: 2 errors (500s) reproduced but both are now handled by new retry patch in feature branch. no secret exfil, no auth bypass found.

security-oncall: created ticket SEC-4521 to increase audit retention and add KMS.Decrypt filter. assigned to @security-oncall and @devops-lead.

maria: PRs: feature/keystore-retry (lin) + fix/keystore-context-check (maria). running CI on both; if green we'll merge and then rollout binding change to prod with a canary.

ashley: sounds good. postmortem note: add to SDLC checklist — any RBAC change to keystore/KMS requires: impact analysis on CI, audit retention check, and pre-warm CI step.

devops-lead: agreed. I'll add a PR template section for keystore/KMS RBAC changes.

maria: thanks all. will follow up when PRs merged and staging proves green. if anyone sees new failures ping here. :thumbsup:

scan-bot: NOTE: thread will auto-close in 72h if no activity.
